records.title: A Code of Practice For Muslims in the West
records.description: A book of practical Islamic rulings (fiqh) written for Muslims living in non-Muslim countries, following the views of Sayyid Ali al-Sistani. Each chapter has a short introduction, general rules, and questions and answers, on topics such as prayer, fasting, food, work, marriage and medical issues.

Is there a book of Islamic rules for Muslims in non-Muslim countries?
Where can I read Ayatollah Sistani's rulings for Muslims in the West?
What does Islam say about everyday life in a non-Muslim country?
Where do I find Shia rulings on food, work and marriage in the West?

records.title: Al-Kāfi (Vol. 1): The Sufficient
records.description: Al-Kafi is a collection of hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) compiled by Shaykh al-Kulayni, shown here in Arabic with an English translation by Muhammad Sarwar. Volume 1 of 8 gathers narrations on intellect and ignorance, the virtue of knowledge, the oneness of God, and those with divine authority; this page also gives an overview of all eight volumes. It is a primary source, best suited to readers who already know the basics.

records.title: Al-Kāfi (Vol. 2): The Sufficient
records.description: Al-Kafi is a collection of hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) compiled by Shaykh al-Kulayni, shown here in Arabic with an English translation by Muhammad Sarwar. Volume 2 of 8 gathers narrations on belief and disbelief, supplication (dua, calling on God), the excellence of the Quran, and social manners. It is a primary source, best suited to readers who already know the basics.
sample_questions: What do Shia hadith say about faith and disbelief?

records.title: Al-Kāfi (Vol. 3): The Sufficient
records.description: Al-Kafi is a collection of hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) compiled by Shaykh al-Kulayni, shown here in Arabic with an English translation by Muhammad Sarwar. Volume 3 of 8 gathers narrations arranged under books on ritual cleansing, menstruation, dying people, prayer and zakat (a religious charity payment). It is a primary source of narrations, not a guide to current rulings, and suits readers with some background.

records.title: Al-Kāfi (Vol. 8): The Sufficient
records.description: Al-Kafi is a collection of hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) compiled by Shaykh al-Kulayni, shown here in Arabic with an English translation by Muhammad Sarwar. Volume 8 of 8, called al-Rawda (the Garden), is a miscellaneous collection that the site says includes long narrations from letters and wills of the Imams and historical reports, not arranged by topic. It is a primary source, best suited to readers with some background.

records.title: Al-Khiṣāl: The Book of Characteristics
records.description: A collection of hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq and arranged by the numbers mentioned in them, from one-numbered characteristics upward; shown in Arabic with an English translation by Dr. Ali Peiravi. According to the site the narrations range over history, doctrine, ethics and jurisprudence. It is a primary source for readers with some background.
sample_questions: What is Al-Khisal by Shaykh Saduq?

records.title: Al-Tawḥīd: The Book of Divine Unity
records.description: A collection of hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) about God, compiled by Shaykh al-Saduq and shown in Arabic with an English translation by Sayed Ali Raza Rizvi. According to the site it covers themes such as God's oneness and attributes, free will and predestination, and the nature of the Quran. It is a primary source for readers who want to see the narrations behind Shia beliefs about God.
sample_questions: What do Shia hadith say about God?
What is the book Al-Tawhid by Shaykh Saduq?
What do the Imams say about free will and predestination?
What hadith are there about God's attributes?

records.title: Kāmil al-Ziyārāt: The Complete Pilgrimage Guide
records.description: A collection of narrations about ziyara, the practice of visiting sacred sites of the Shia, compiled by Ibn Qulawayh al-Qummi and shown in Arabic with an English translation by Sayyid Mohsen Al-Husayni Al-Milani. According to the site it covers the purposes of ziyara, the rewards and etiquette of visiting, and the recitations to read, with most of the book about visiting Imam Husayn. It is a primary source rather than an introduction.

records.title: Kitāb al-Ghayba: The Book of Occultation
records.description: A book by Shaykh al-Tusi on the occultation (ghayba, meaning being hidden from view) of the twelfth Imam, al-Mahdi; shown in Arabic with an English translation by Sayyid Athar Husain S. H. Rizvi. According to the site it combines arguments and hadith (reported sayings of the Prophet and the Imams) on the occultation, the Imam's deputies and the signs of his return. It is a detailed primary source for readers with some background.

records.title: Nahj al-Balāgha: The Peak of Eloquence
records.description: A collection of the sermons, letters and short sayings of Imam Ali, compiled by al-Sharif al-Radi and shown in Arabic with an English translation by Sayed Ali Raza. The page is divided into three parts: Sermons, Letters and Sayings. It is a primary text rather than an introduction.

records.title: Risālat al-Ḥuqūq: Treatise of Rights
records.description: A short treatise on the rights a person owes to God, to society, to family and to their own body, which the site presents as attributed to Imam Zayn al-Abidin; shown in Arabic with an English translation by William C. Chittick. It is brief and covers everyday duties toward others.
